"Those counts, amounts, and effective windows match DealerDrop files DF-00020 and DF-00040 ... cash=ledger, difference $0, duplicate_source_event_ids=0, 8/8 and 9/9 accepted, status RECONCILED."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "West dealers switched from same-day files in Jan–Feb to month-end files from March."
"The 21:xx clock matches the 21:15 DealerDrop job. Non-West dealers post annuals same-day, so this is a West intake cycle, not a broken writer."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"Entitlement ledger (not in extract). Decision changes if any of the 17 IDs already had an overlapping 365-day entitlement for the same source_event_id."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not reverse or re-upload DF-00020 / DF-00040. Rebuild the flagged weekly pack on effective_event_date (or tag dealer annual batches)"
"Reopen only if that sample or the entitlement ledger shows a second recognition of the same event."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material issue. The West 31 May annual cluster is delayed posting of unique dealer renewals, not duplicate revenue, stuffed reporting, or a pipeline defect."
"Sample the 17 source_event_ids against dealer cash sheets."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Duplicate revenue — rejected" is somewhat too definitive because the submission has not checked the entitlement ledger and identifies a possible matching non-dealer UPI settlement as unresolved.
"No material issue" is stronger than the evidence warrants until dealer cash sheets, entitlement overlap, and the UPI row are checked.
"Pipeline defect — rejected" is well supported for the import and posting process, but the reconciliation tests do not by themselves rule out every downstream data-pipeline defect.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The strongest alternative is duplicate or overlapping entitlement recognition despite unique source_event_ids, particularly through an existing entitlement or the possible matching non-dealer UPI settlement. The analyst handled this as a decision-changing unknown, but did not fully test it before stating the headline conclusion.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and document the entitlement-ledger and UPI cross-checks for all 17 source_event_ids, alongside the dealer cash-sheet sample, before describing duplicate revenue as rejected rather than provisional.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South tickets fell after cutover; N/W/E daily rates did not show a matching drop" — tickets.csv (pre/post 10 May; Apr 10–May 9 vs May 10–Jun 9)
"Post-pilot South IVR: transfer ~3.3%, case link ~3.5%, abandon+error ~40.5%, ~24% end at authenticate" — ivr_interactions.jsonl (region=S, started_at ≥ 10 May)

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Do not treat the South ticket drop as proof that NovaIVR improved customer experience"

"Farah’s 18 May email defines containment only after authentication and keeps pre-auth exits out of CareDesk; under Nova, transfers/case-creation collapse (~50% → ~3.5%) while ~40.5% of sessions end ABANDONED/ERROR"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Some real self-service exists (~44% resolve at balance_check / pack_info / self_service), so the pilot is not empty"
"Unknowns: exact CareDesk case-creation rule under Nova; whether RESOLVED at authenticate / issue_menu is a fixed issue or a soft exit; CSAT / sampled-call outcomes for abandon/error sessions"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Hold national expansion. Keep South as a bounded pilot."
"Re-decide expansion only after those gates improve — not when CareDesk volume alone looks quiet."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Fix authentication (TOKEN_MISMATCH, ANI_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT) and rebuild the pilot scorecard to include pre-auth exits, error rate, repeat no-case callers, and a short post-session sample/CSAT for two complete weeks."
"Interview Farah Iqbal (Customer Care Operations) with these five questions"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that "transfers/case-creation collapse (~50% → ~3.5%)" may conflate a transfer or case-link metric with actual CareDesk case creation; the exact field definitions should be shown.

The claim that "Network incidents do not uniquely explain a South-only sustained ticket decline" is plausible and cited to service_events.csv, but the submission does not provide the event dates, severity, or comparison calculation needed to reproduce that exclusion.

The phrase "national rollout remains unsafe" is a strong operational characterization; the evidence clearly makes expansion unjustified or premature, but does not establish that every form of controlled expansion would be unsafe.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The South ticket decline could partly reflect genuine self-service success or successful deflection rather than capture failure. The analyst handled this by identifying approximately 44% of sessions as resolved at substantive stages and by preserving the possibility that agent/app ticket declines represent successful deflection, while correctly treating those outcomes as unverified.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible joined analysis with exact field definitions and cohorts for case creation, pre-auth exits, repeat no-case subscribers, and later tickets, then link or sample those journeys to verified resolution outcomes so abandonment is not treated as a complaint by implication.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific fields and values: “2026-05-27→2026-06-04,” “INV-09 TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED,” and “INV-17 COMM_LINK_WARN; cleared; impact_mw=0.”
It distinguishes uncertainty by labeling the export-volume and recovery-event claims “Medium” confidence and the severity claim “Low” confidence.
Traceability is good, but the submission does not identify source filenames or provide a more direct extract reference beyond the event fields.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It tests a plausible innocent explanation for the thin event set by proposing: “confirm this is the full extract for the window (row count / filter rules).”
It identifies a discriminating check for the communications mechanism: “INV-17 data continuity around 2026-05-27 09:42.”
It rejects the plant-wide reliability hypothesis using the observed pattern: “four distinct inverters, one event each, all cleared=yes, all impact_mw=0.”
The reasoning is sound but does not actually triangulate an independent channel; the proposed completeness and continuity checks remain future work.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly avoids escalation: “I would not escalate equipment failure from this alone.”
It scopes the conclusion carefully: “nothing here alone supports equipment failure, intent, or commercial impact.”
It identifies what would change the assessment—export completeness and INV-17 continuity—rather than using a generic request for more data.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommended action is proportionate: “Perform one cheap check (export completeness / expected row count).”
It preserves operational restraint by recommending: “Stop on escalation.”
The conditional follow-up for INV-17 continuity is a useful, low-cost test tied to the only potentially consequential event.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly reflects the visible pattern of four events, zero stated MW impact, cleared status, and no repeated inverter IDs.
It does not invent a plant problem from the isolated seven-minute communications warning.
It appropriately treats the unmatched recovery event as a data-quality/completeness question rather than proof of equipment failure.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Observed: four rows spanning 2026-05-27 through 2026-06-04, with the cited inverter IDs and event fields, subject to the supplied extract being complete.

Inferred: “TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED ... implies a prior fault.” The label suggests an earlier condition but does not prove that a fault occurred within the supplied window or that it was a plant problem.

Inferred but appropriately tentative: “Comm warnings can coincide with telemetry gaps.” This is a plausible mechanism, not evidence that a gap actually occurred here; the submission correctly proposes checking continuity.

Potentially overstated by omission: “all cleared=yes, all impact_mw=0” supports the scoped in-file conclusion, but cannot establish absence of impact outside the extract or beyond the recorded impact field.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent thinness and unmatched recovery event may result from a partial or filtered export rather than plant behavior; independently, the isolated COMM_LINK_WARN may represent a short telemetry interruption with no production consequence. These alternatives are more consistent with the zero-MW, cleared event pattern than a plant-wide inverter reliability issue.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform and report the export-completeness check first—expected row count, time-window filters, and whether all event types are included—then use INV-17 telemetry continuity only if that check confirms the extract is complete.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific fields and files: “`dispatch_blocks.csv` Σ`dsm_penalty_rs`,” “`schedule_source`, base vs submitted,” and “DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf.”
It distinguishes the observed day-over-day result from the inferred causal claim: “It is not defensible as proof the pilot caused a 31.6% cut.”
The same-day counterfactual is explicitly constructed from `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May, with the reported Rs 549,569 versus Rs 453,086 comparison.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission notices the different-day comparison and separates the 29 May same-day pilot effect from weather, operations, and non-STOW differences: “the rest (~Rs 113k) reflects differences between the two days.”
It triangulates DSM penalties, schedule revisions, generation, schedule-generation gaps, and DSM pricing bands rather than relying only on the impact note.

It tests the output-improvement explanation using the STOW comparison: “STOW generation ~1,002 MWh vs 28 May ~1,113 MWh,” and identifies forecast accuracy, tracker behavior, curtailment, and weather differences as unresolved confounders.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission labels the full causal attribution “Low” confidence while labeling the arithmetic and counterfactual replay “High” confidence.
It accurately limits the conclusion: “It does not support scaling on a single before/after pair or attributing the full 31.6% to the pilot.”
It explicitly states what remains unidentified and proposes additional high-wind events and alternating pilot on/off conditions.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Continue limited pilot use” preserves the observed potential value without treating the single comparison as proven ROI.
The recommendation retains operational constraints by applying revisions only “when forecast/tracker logic supports them.”
The proposed paired block-level settlement replay and eventual pilot on/off alternation is a discriminating next test, not merely a generic request for more data.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion preserves the smaller same-day benefit: “~Rs 96,500 DSM” avoided versus the 29 May base schedule, while rejecting attribution of the full 31.6%.
It correctly characterizes 31.6% as “an observational benchmark, not causal effect size.”
It reaches the appropriately scoped conclusion that stow-aware downward revisions can reduce DSM on high-wind days, while stopping short of claiming proven scale-up economics.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement “Rejected: Pilot increased generation” is somewhat too strong causally. Lower STOW-window generation on 29 May is an observed comparison, but it does not by itself establish that the pilot could not have increased generation because day-level weather, tracker, curtailment, and operational differences remain unidentified.

“Savings came mainly from better schedule–actual alignment at high DSM bands” is plausible and supported by the gap calculation and DSM-band schedule, but the submission could show a block-level decomposition to establish “mainly” quantitatively.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The same-day replay may show that the revised schedules would have reduced penalties under the realized actuals, but it does not fully establish how the pilot would perform across different wind, forecast, tracker, curtailment, or operational conditions. The observed benefit could therefore be real but event-specific and partly dependent on the unusually favorable realized profile.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a block-level decomposition of the Rs 96,500 same-day counterfactual savings by STOW block and DSM band, alongside paired pilot-on/pilot-off or base-versus-revision settlement results across at least three comparable high-wind events. This would test both the stated mechanism and its generalizability.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the core conclusion to specific sources: "Swiss matrix P1001 approved code is **90211000**, effective 2025-01-01" and "Matrix Read Me: EU uses CN8; Switzerland uses a local tariff code; **matching strings across jurisdictions is not expected.**"
It identifies source limitations, including that the product-master snapshot is "commercial, not a customs ruling" and that the Swiss matrix says to "confirm Tares/ruling for legal use."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly tests alternatives under "Rejected Hypotheses," including "Likely broker miscode vs Helios," "Wrong product / origin / value," "Duty evasion," and "Stale Swiss code."
It does not treat the flag alone as dispositive: "The Helios **90211090** flag is an expected EU/Helios vs Swiss string mismatch, not proof the filing is wrong."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The submission distinguishes confidence by source and labels the auto-flag as "Medium" confidence.
It expressly identifies unresolved uncertainty: "A Tares extract or Swiss BTI/ruling" is missing, as are "The comparison spec" and the "Nomenclature version on the declaration form."
Its duty conclusion is appropriately qualified: "not supported" rather than asserting that a duty issue is impossible.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the jurisdictional mechanism: "EU uses CN8; Switzerland uses a local tariff code; **matching strings across jurisdictions is not expected.**"
It identifies a data-lineage/schema failure: "Schema v0.3 stores a single 8-character hts_code and does **not** model code-system, nomenclature version, or ruling authority."
It connects the ERP value and local classification: "Helios is an 8-character ERP value" while the Swiss matrix supplies the country working classification.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommendation is proportionate to the evidence: "Do not escalate CH-2025-000522 as a likely Swiss declaration error."
The submission preserves an appropriate legal safeguard by listing "A Tares extract or Swiss BTI/ruling ... for legal use" as missing evidence.
The action could more explicitly require that validation before final compliance closure, rather than only declining escalation.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Declared **90211000** matches the Swiss working code for P1001" is supported by the Swiss matrix, but it should not be read as proof of legally correct classification because the submission itself notes that the matrix is not a customs ruling and requires Tares/ruling confirmation.

"Stale Swiss code after the July 2025 EU P1001 update - rejected" is reasonable for the jurisdiction-mismatch hypothesis, but the conclusion remains dependent on the matrix's completeness and authority; the missing Tares/BTI evidence limits a definitive legal conclusion.
The text "EU 90211010?90211090 change" is malformed or ambiguous and should be corrected to the exact source codes and transition date.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss working matrix or its effective-date/versioning could be incomplete or non-authoritative, so 90211000 might still require confirmation through Tares or a Swiss ruling; alternatively, the automated rule may have been intended to compare a Swiss-local code but was configured against the Helios EU code because the schema lacks jurisdiction and nomenclature fields.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the 2025-11-04 Tares extract or Swiss BTI/ruling, and document the comparison-rule specification showing that Swiss-local classification—not the Helios EU CN8 string—was the intended field.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Irish declaration IE-2025-000411, 2025-09-18, status Accepted... declared origin United States... Preference = Yes."
"SUP-02 / P1006 Ireland... valid_to 2025-07-31, status Expired in register."
"Register search: no current document... Explicitly does not prove no paper exists off-register."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Zero duty can be MFN or preference; this packet has no Irish rate table. Zero duty does not prove originating status."
"No register hit means no supplier declaration exists anywhere — rejected."
"US manufacturing country / Helios COO supports the preference tick — rejected."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The actual supplier declaration... for this shipment" is identified as missing.
"Whether a post-31 Jul 2025 Irish (or other EU) declaration exists in category folders but was never loaded..."
"Do not treat the claim as cleared."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Helios manufacturing country was not designed to prove preference. COO is overloaded."
"Register is not always updated when sourcing changes."
"Using ERP when the document is blank is for extraction testing, not for clearing a preference claim."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold the preference claim."
"Ask the broker/procurement to produce a supplier declaration... valid on 2025-09-18 for the actual P1006 producer, then link it in ClearView."
"If no in-force originating document appears, instruct a preference-to-No correction and reassess duty; leave the Accepted declaration otherwise unchanged."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The opening statement says "origin on the declaration and invoice is United States," but the submission's own evidence table correctly states that the invoice identifies "manufacturing country, not preferential origin." The invoice therefore supports US manufacturing country, not necessarily US preferential origin; this wording should be corrected.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may still be supportable if an in-force supplier declaration or equivalent originating statement for the actual P1006 producer existed on 2025-09-18 but was omitted from the packet, category folders, register, or ClearView. The evidence supports withholding clearance, not declaring the claim invalid or fraudulent.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Correct the opening invoice-origin wording and obtain and verify the shipment-specific supplier declaration, actual producer identity, and broker's legal preference basis before deciding whether to correct the declaration.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"QCore analytics snapshot refreshes daily at ~02:10"
"30 RELEASED rows have coa_status MISSING (17) or INDEX_PENDING (13)"
"LabTrack extract is 48h lag ... vs QCore 2026-07-31" — the cited source dates support a freshness mismatch, although the stated 48-hour interval appears overstated.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning

"Separately, Ops’ ‘~1.5 days’ aligns more with receipt → release ... than the SOP routine clock"
"02:10 is just when Quality works the night shift ... far more consistent with a load job ... still falsifiable by the audit check above"

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "do not use the apparent cycle time ... until verified"
"If extract time ≠ audit time, treat the extract as reporting lag, not cycle time"
"What Would Change the Decision" specifies audit-time agreement, a documented evidence-available timestamp, and reconciliation of CertVault semantics before dashboard use.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "do not use the apparent cycle time from batch_release.csv as a performance KPI until verified"
"Smallest verification: Pick 5–10 released batches ... and compare extract qcore_release_ts to the live QCore disposition / authorization audit timestamp"
"If that holds, a routine KPI dashboard is reasonable — still not on raw receipt→release"

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "‘Nothing smells; build the dashboard on receipt→qcore_release_ts.’ Rejected"
"‘Use lab_complete→release and you’re fine.’ Rejected"
"‘02:10 is just when Quality works the night shift.’ Rejected as unverified"
The submission states what audit evidence would revive the timestamp-validity interpretation.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Pick 5–10 released batches ... include at least one RELEASED+MISSING COA ... and compare extract qcore_release_ts to the live QCore disposition / authorization audit timestamp"
"Evidence that qcore_release_ts equals the QCore authorization audit time for a stratified sample ... plus a documented ‘evidence available’ timestamp"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the LabTrack extract is "48h lag" is not directly supported by the cited snapshot timestamps of 2026-07-29T23:00 and 2026-07-31T02:10, which are approximately 27 hours apart unless a different comparison reference is intended.

The inference that 02:10 is an interface load time is strong and appropriately framed as a fit/hypothesis, but it remains unconfirmed until the authorization audit timestamp or event definition is checked.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 timestamps could represent genuine authorizations performed through a scheduled operational process rather than reporting lag; the decisive test is whether qcore_release_ts matches the underlying QCore authorization/disposition audit event for a stratified sample, including non-02:10 records.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain the QCore event or authorization audit log and its timestamp-field definition, then reconcile it with qcore_release_ts for a stratified sample while recording the actual evidence-available time and source snapshot times; correct the LabTrack lag calculation before quantifying the impact.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Same MPN, divergent descriptions across sites" cited to spare_parts.csv with concrete examples PMP-2288, VLV-3722, BRG-1507, SNS-9910, and MTR-4401; "Several high-value servo hits sit on reserved_for_critical_asset=true" cited to part_restrictions.csv plus spare_parts.csv; "MaintStar-global snapshot is monthly / 2026-06-26" cited to source_freshness.csv.

"Value split (of $152,558): Actionable now ~$12.4k (8%) | Needs check ~$58.5k (38%) | Not transferable ~$81.7k (54%)" is linked to specific request and inventory examples, and the submission acknowledges stale and conflicting source data.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Semantic similarity finds candidates, but catalog equivalence is not transferability" is operationalized through revision, qualification, reservation, and live-CMMS checks rather than treating a text match as a cause of avoidable spend.
The rejected hypotheses test the alternatives that an MPN match is automatically actionable and that there is no opportunity because descriptions are already normalized.
The reasoning is strong but does not fully demonstrate candidate-by-candidate UOM, qualification, shelf-life, or temporal reconciliation, so the mechanism is not completely established.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "from current evidence only: ~8% actionable now" and "~38% needs engineering / live-CMMS check" appropriately distinguish current evidence from confirmed transferability.
"MaintStar-global snapshot is monthly / 2026-06-26 while local CMMS is live" and "ProcureNet open-request export is weekly" make source freshness decision-relevant.
The labels "Actionable now" and "Not transferable" remain somewhat too definitive given the stale inventory snapshot and the stated need to confirm that requests were not already issued or reserved.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not fund a pilot on a headline '$150k+ savings'; cap near-term avoidable-purchase claims at the same-site slice until live availability is confirmed" materially reframes the decision from savings estimation to controlled discovery.
"search pilot can help discovery" and "It does not justify treating the full open-request quote pool ... as avoidable buy value" protect against unsafe automation and overstatement.
The recommendation is practical and reversible, but it does not specify pilot success criteria, an execution owner, or a precise workflow for preventing duplicate issuance while checks are pending.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects three plausible alternatives: "Semantic search means most of ~$153k open quotes are avoidable purchases," "Any MPN match with available_qty_global>0 is actionable savings now," and "No opportunity - descriptions are already normalized."
It gives evidence for each rejection through reservations, revision mismatches, SITE_SPECIFIC_CHECK, stale quantities, and same-site open buys.
It identifies what would change the estimate, but the competing explanation that same-site matches may also be stale or already consumed is only flagged for confirmation rather than tested.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Live CMMS on-hand/available/reservation for the candidate part_ids (not the June MaintStar extract)" is a focused, high-value request.

The submission also specifies discriminating evidence: "engineer sign-off on rev-A vs rev-B VLV-3722 and on HEPA SITE_SPECIFIC_CHECK rows" and confirmation that same-site lines were not already issued or reserved.
It explains the decision impact: the avoidable estimate rises if live stock clears and engineering accepts the needs-check pool, and falls if reservations expand.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The ~$12.4k labeled "Actionable now" is not fully confirmed because the cited MaintStar inventory is stale and the submission itself says issuance or reservation status still needs confirmation.

The ~$81.7k labeled "Not transferable" may be an overstatement from the available extract: critical reservations and zero quantity establish that those rows are not currently actionable on the shown evidence, but they do not prove no later release, substitute, or engineering-approved alternative exists.
The recommendation to "hold/cancel the buy" for same-site matches could create operational risk unless live CMMS status and request ownership are checked immediately before cancellation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The evidence supports semantic search as a useful candidate generator, but the true actionable opportunity may be materially above or below 8%. A live, timestamp-aligned CMMS query could release some currently reserved or apparently unavailable stock, while stale same-site records could eliminate part of the claimed near-term opportunity. The submission's directional conclusion is sound, but its current value split should be treated as a provisional classification rather than a confirmed financial estimate.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run one timestamped live-CMMS reconciliation for all 24 open requests and every candidate part_id, joined on manufacturer part number plus revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and current available quantity; use the result to validate or revise the 8% actionable floor before any buy cancellation or savings claim.
